title: IMM-Core: Interview Metadata Model — Core Profile
description: IMM-Core v1.0. Generic, discipline-agnostic metadata schema for interview-based qualitative research. Implementation Profiles (e.g. IMM-Profile-LuxOH, IMM-Profile-Migration) extend this Core without weakening its constraints. Block D (preservation fields) and full speaker components are deferred to Phase 2. Single source of truth: tap/core.csv.

record_id.description: Block A. Stable identifier. Recommended format: YYYY-MM-DD_{INSTITUTION_CODE}_{NNNN}. Pattern not enforced at Core; see Implementation Profile for institution-specific constraints.

interviewer.description: Block A. Name of interviewer. ORCID may follow in parentheses, e.g. 'Jane Smith (0000-0001-2345-6789)'.

consent_status.description: Block A. GDPR-based consent category. Free string at Core; see vocabs/consent_status.md for recommended vocabulary. Implementation Profiles may impose a controlled enum.

accessRights.description: Block A. Repository-level access rights. Uses cross-domain OpenAIRE/Zenodo/DataCite terms.

title.description: Block B. Interview title or descriptive label.

interviewee_display.description: Block B. Pseudonym or display name. Core-level minimal speaker hook. Full speaker component deferred to Phase 2.

language.description: Block B. ISO 639-3 three-letter language code, e.g. 'eng', 'deu', 'fra'. Single language only at Core; multilingual interviews deferred to Phase 2.

spatial.description: Block B. Place of interview. Free string at Core; recommend using a controlled vocabulary appropriate to the discipline and geography.

keywords.description: Block B. Subject keywords. Free string array at Core; profiles SHOULD specify a controlled vocabulary.

abstract.description: Block B. Short descriptive (non-analytic) summary, 2–3 sentences. Describes the interview as a research object. See methodological-positions/abstracts.md.

timecoded_segments.description: Block C. Array of segment objects with required sub-properties.

related_materials.description: Block C. URLs or persistent identifiers (DOI, handle) of related materials — transcripts, companion documents, derived files.
